Other Important Information:
If there are insufficient funds in the positions designated in your primary withdrawal instructions, you have instructed us to attempt to make the distribution through the liquidation of core positions, including money market core positions in the same account, then beginning with the non-core money market position with the lowest balance. If sufficient funds are not available from these positions, you have instructed us to attempt to make the distribution by making funds available through the liquidation of bond or equity fund positions in the same account, beginning with the bond or equity fund positions with the lowest balance. If two eligible positions have identical balances, we will liquidate the fund with the lowest CUSIP (security identifier). We will then attempt to make any remaining distributions from other accounts in the plan in the following order: mutual fund accounts first, then brokerage accounts, then accounts managed by Personalized Portfolios. If the plan includes Personalized Portfolios account(s), Personalized Portfolios will make every effort to maintain the appropriate asset allocation of your Personalized Portfolios account.
We will only liquidate from the mutual fund(s) you have designated as your funding withdrawal method. If there are insufficient funds to meet your scheduled distribution, a partial distribution may be sent.
Fidelity will place liquidating trades for the requested dollar amount needed for your scheduled distribution. These trades may be placed up to 2 days prior to the scheduled date of distribution to allow for trade settlement.
Back-end loads, redemption fees or transaction fees may result in the actual distribution amount to be less than requested.
Distributions may take place earlier or later than the scheduled date due to holidays or other market closings. Distribution payments scheduled to pay out on the 29th, 30th or 31st that fall in a month that has less days will be paid out on the last business day of the month.
Separate confirmation statements will not be produced for your brokerage distributions.
